question: the three aged-zone tests on FX, metals and Deriv synthetics: does a fresh, long-waiting, untested zone deliver (aged_zone_rule.json), does a slow return with the higher timeframe aligned (aged_context_rule.json), and does sizing the stop to volatility at the return change it (aged_volstop_rule.json)
rules: each test's zones, fills, exits, walks, attributes and pass conditions unchanged; only the data differs
data: the broker's bars (mt5bt), 4h and 1d. Judged: FX_UNSEEN (AUDUSD USDCAD USDCHF NZDUSD EURJPY GBPJPY EURGBP AUDJPY USDCNH), METAL_UNSEEN (XAGUSD XPTUSD XPDUSD XCUUSD), DERIV_DIFFUSIVE (the volatility, step and drift-switch indices). Reported, not judged: FX_SEEN (EURUSD GBPUSD USDJPY) and XAUUSD (in the in-sample MT5 set where the aged pattern was read), DERIV_JUMPY (Boom, Crash, Jump, Range Break: bar fills miss their jumps)

primaries.aged: ALL origins, wait >= 10 days, E1: R > 0 with 90% interval above 0, both halves, above iid and GARCH walks, above wait < 2 days
primaries.context: ALL origins, SLOW & ALIGNED, any wait, E1: R > 0 with interval above 0, both halves, above both walks, above the rest
primaries.volstop: ALL origins, wait >= 10 days, V1, E1: R > 0 with interval above 0, both halves, above both walks, above V1 with wait < 2 days

multiplicity: 3 tests x 3 judged sets = 9 verdicts; a single pass is reported as such, not as a finding, unless it also passes in a second set
expectation_deriv: Deriv's diffusive synthetics are published iid generators: every number should equal its walk's
